decisive_items: Vitreous biopsy: Hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm, small to medium-sized cells with scant cytoplasm and oval, pleomorphic, hyperchromatic nuclei
Immunohistochemistry: Positive for glial fibrillary acid protein, oligodendrocyte transcription factor 2, mutant IDH-1 protein, p53; Loss of ATRX protein; Ki-67 proliferation index ~10%
Diffuse enlargement of orbital portion of right optic nerve, enhancement of nerve sheath, slight flattening of posterior globe
response.rationale: Vitreous biopsy and immunohistochemistry confirm an astrocytic neoplasm with IDH-mutant and ATRX-loss features, establishing glioma as the underlying diagnosis; the vascular and inflammatory findings are secondary or nonspecific.

rejected.why: Imaging shows optic nerve enlargement and enhancement, but the biopsy-proven astrocytic neoplasm excludes a purely idiopathic inflammatory process.
Central retinal artery occlusion is a secondary vascular complication of the optic nerve process, not the primary diagnosis.
Immunotherapy context is relevant but the definitive vitreous biopsy findings demonstrate a neoplastic glioma rather than a purely immune-related adverse event.
